name: Christopher of Bavaria
role: Scandinavian king under the Kalmar Union
contribution: King of Denmark, Sweden, and Norway during the Kalmar Union.
legacy: As a whole his rule, according to the politics of the nobility and his succession, might be called the start of the long period of balance between royal power and nobility which lasted until 1660.

checks.lead: Christopher of Bavaria (Danish and Norwegian: Christoffer; Swedish: Kristofer; 26 February 1416 – 5/6 January 1448) was King of Denmark (1440–1448, as Christopher III), Sweden (1441–1448), and Norway (1442–1448) during the Kalmar Union. He ruled after the Kalmar Union's King Erik of Pomerania was deposed. Early in his reign, he put down two peasant rebellions in Funen and Jutland. He was disliked by the Swedish nobles, as they pointed to his inability to manage harvest failures and to stop Erik's plundering. They also questioned his foreign background.
